summary: Gaisirt Imaging Systems, Inc., a manufacturer of MRI and CT systems, engaged Beputh Field Services, LLC under a New York-law Master Services Agreement effective March 1, 2024. Beputh provides installation, preventive maintenance and field service on Gaisirt scanners installed at hospital sites. Beputh's obligations are guaranteed by its parent, Beputh Holdings Corp. The folder holds the MSA, the parent guaranty, a data processing addendum, the pre-signing term sheet, a quality agreement, Order Form No. 3, Amendment No. 1, and Gaisirt's October 20, 2026 letter to Beputh. That letter objects to a 7% rate increase and discloses Gaisirt's pending merger into Kelderman Health Technologies N.V. Two distractors are included: Gaisirt's Rochester service-depot lease and Beputh's certificate of insurance. Six issues are planted. Three are cross-document: an expired 30-day rate-objection window, an unaddressed change-of-control consent triggered by the Kelderman merger, and an uncapped client indemnity created by the DPA through the MSA's cap carve-out. The other three are an unrestricted assignment right for Beputh, a narrowed 'Complaint' definition in the controlling quality agreement, and a Delaware law and forum clause in the parent guaranty.

issues.label: unrestricted assignment
issues.description: MSA Section 15.1 bars only Gaisirt from assigning without Beputh's prior written consent. It then states that Provider may freely assign the MSA and any Order Form to any person without consent, so Beputh could transfer the service relationship to a competing imaging OEM or a weaker service vendor. The term sheet (D4, Assignment) recorded a mutual restriction allowing only affiliate transfers without consent. Nothing in Amendment No. 1 or any other document restores that restriction. The parent guaranty (D2) guarantees the obligations of Beputh Field Services, LLC, so an assignee's performance may fall outside the guaranty.
detect_terms: Customer shall not assign or transfer
issues.expected_finding: MSA Section 15.1 lets Beputh assign the MSA and Order Forms to anyone, including a Gaisirt competitor, without consent, contrary to the mutual consent-with-affiliate-exception term in the term sheet, and should be amended to make the restriction mutual.

issues.label: expired notice window
issues.description: MSA Section 4.4 lets Beputh adjust rates once per contract year by a Rate Adjustment Notice. Customer may object within 30 days after receipt and then terminate the affected Order Form. If Customer does not object in time, the adjustment is deemed accepted. Gaisirt's letter (D6), dated October 20, 2026, objects to the 7% increase in Beputh's Rate Adjustment Notice dated September 4, 2026. The letter states that Gaisirt received that notice on September 8, 2026. Read together, the 30-day window closed on October 8, 2026, twelve days before Gaisirt's objection. The increase applies to the $3,840,000 annual fee under Order Form No. 3 (D7). D6 shows Gaisirt still disputes the increase, and no document records acceptance.
issues.expected_finding: Gaisirt's October 20, 2026 objection came after the 30-day objection window under MSA Section 4.4 closed on October 8, 2026 (measured from its stated September 8, 2026 receipt of Beputh's notice), so the 7% increase is exposed to being deemed accepted and Gaisirt's objection and termination rights are at risk unless it obtains Beputh's written waiver or a negotiated amendment.
detect_terms2: hereby objects to the rate increase

issues.label: change of control consent
issues.description: MSA Section 15.3 is a mutual clause. A Change of Control of either Party (acquisition of more than 50% of voting equity, including by merger) is deemed an assignment. For Customer, that requires Provider's prior written consent under Section 15.1. Without consent, Provider may terminate the MSA and all Order Forms on 30 days' notice. Gaisirt's October 20, 2026 letter (D6) tells Beputh that Gaisirt signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Kelderman Health Technologies N.V. on October 2, 2026. Under that agreement Gaisirt will become a wholly owned Kelderman subsidiary, and closing is expected in February 2027. The letter does not request Beputh's consent, and no other document records consent or a waiver. Read alone, neither provision shows a problem. Together they show the merger will trigger a consent right that has not been addressed, during an active rate dispute that gives Beputh leverage.
detect_terms: Change of Control of either Party shall be deemed an assignment
issues.expected_finding: The Kelderman merger disclosed in Gaisirt's October 20, 2026 letter is a Change of Control deemed an assignment under MSA Section 15.3, so Gaisirt needs Beputh's prior written consent before the expected February 2027 closing or Beputh may terminate the MSA and all Order Forms on 30 days' notice.

issues.label: uncapped indemnity
issues.description: MSA Section 12.1 caps each party's liability at fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months. Section 12.3 excludes from that cap 'a Party's obligations under Section 11'. Section 11.4 provides that any indemnity in an Addendum forms part of Section 11. On its own the MSA is ordinary: Section 11 contains only narrow mutual IP and bodily-injury indemnities. DPA Section 8.2, also ordinary on its face, makes Gaisirt indemnify, defend and hold harmless Beputh against all losses arising from or relating to Customer Personal Data or Customer's processing instructions. Those losses include HIPAA and state regulatory fines and patient claims. Read together, Section 11.4 pulls the DPA indemnity into Section 11, and Section 12.3 removes it from the cap. Gaisirt's broadest indemnity is therefore uncapped. The order of precedence (MSA Section 2.3) gives the DPA priority on Personal Data matters, and nothing reconciles the cap.
detect_terms: shall not apply to a Party's obligations under Section 11
issues.expected_finding: Because MSA Section 11.4 incorporates Addendum indemnities into Section 11 and Section 12.3 excludes Section 11 obligations from the cap, Gaisirt's broad indemnity of Beputh in DPA Section 8.2 for Personal Data losses, including regulatory fines and patient claims, is uncapped and should be brought within the cap or a defined super-cap.
detect_terms2: Customer shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Provider

issues.label: defined term inconsistency
issues.description: MSA Section 1.1 defines 'Complaint' broadly as any written, electronic or oral communication alleging a deficiency in a Covered System's safety, quality or performance. Beputh must forward Complaints to Gaisirt within two Business Days. Quality Agreement Sections 1.1 and 5.2 define 'Complaint' only as a written allegation involving actual or alleged patient injury, and they impose the forwarding duty only for that narrow category. MSA Section 2.3 gives the Quality Agreement priority over the MSA on quality and regulatory matters, so the narrow definition controls. As a result, Beputh need not pass on oral complaints or non-injury performance complaints. Gaisirt must still capture and evaluate those complaints as the manufacturer under FDA's 21 CFR Part 820 complaint-handling requirements.
detect_terms: involving actual or alleged patient injury
issues.expected_finding: Because the Quality Agreement controls on quality matters under MSA Section 2.3, its narrow 'Complaint' definition (written allegations of patient injury only) overrides the MSA's broad definition, so Beputh need not forward oral or non-injury complaints that Gaisirt must handle under 21 CFR Part 820, and the Quality Agreement definition should be conformed to the MSA.

issues.label: governing law mismatch
issues.description: Parent Guaranty Section 9 provides that the guaranty is governed by Delaware law. It submits all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware Court of Chancery. The MSA it supports chooses New York law and the exclusive jurisdiction of New York County courts (MSA Sections 17.1 and 17.2). The MSA's order of precedence (Section 2.3) covers only the MSA, its Amendments, the Quality Agreement, the DPA and Order Forms. Beputh Holdings Corp. is not a party to the MSA, so nothing reconciles the two clauses. To recover a single service failure, Gaisirt would have to sue Beputh in New York and the guarantor in Delaware, which risks duplicative proceedings and inconsistent results.
detect_terms: laws of the State of Delaware
issues.expected_finding: The parent guaranty's Delaware law and exclusive Delaware Court of Chancery forum conflict with the MSA's New York law and New York County forum and are not reconciled by the MSA's precedence clause, forcing Gaisirt to pursue Beputh and its guarantor in separate forums, so the guaranty should be amended to New York law and forum.
